title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Chart Table. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. This world will govern the client tracking page, Admin, and Tracker tools.

options.label: Chart Table
options.lineage: Harbor chart table with glassine overlays and plotted courses
options.thesis: Every company board is a lit chart table: shipments are plotted courses, not dashboard cards.
options.viewport: Ronin’s public board: a pale chart ground, tracking numbers as glassine slips on the left, a plotted Google Map as the chart itself, facts and timed travel history as pencil notes on the selected course.
options.risk: Reads as a map widget glued to a list if the paper, overlays, and course ink do not own the whole viewport.

raised.raise: Selecting one tracking number is one pull: map, facts, and history lock as one linked field.
Status color lives only as a hairline fringe and course tint; the chart body stays paper.
The selected shipment comes forward; others recede; the selected board holds still.
The plotted course is a persistent trace on a measured chart grid; selection triggers and holds it.
Travel history is a timed sequential list that fills its allotted column exactly.

options.label: Progress Strips
options.thesis: Each FedEx number is a paper strip in a bay: waypoints stamped across, the live one pulled forward.
options.viewport: A metal bay of shipment strips; the selected strip expands to show Google Map, facts, and a stamped waypoint history.
options.risk: Also the direction most logistics-tracking runs land on: familiar control-room, easy to flatten into a table.

options.label: Night Console
options.thesis: Graphite panels with hairline seams: tracking numbers, map, facts, and history as persistent tiles.
options.viewport: A tiled ops surface: shipment list, Google Map, facts, and history persist; selection changes contents, not layout.
options.case: Holds product clarity for Admin and Tracker; loses audience identification for Ronin’s public clients versus a chart table.
options.risk: Slips into a generic dark SaaS dashboard if syntax color and hairlines are not strict.

options.label: Miura Packet
options.thesis: A compact packet that unfolds into a linked field of shipment cells.
options.viewport: A gold packet unfolds into a parallelogram grid of tracking cells.
options.case: Logistics clients do not identify with origami packets; unfolding hides the live board.
options.kept: One control propagates across every linked cell.
options.risk: The fold becomes decoration instead of navigation.

options.label: Iridescent Edge
options.thesis: A white field with status only as a mint-rose-violet fringe.
options.viewport: Wide white margins; shipment data stays achromatic; color only at status edges.
options.case: Weather optics do not read as freight location.
options.kept: Color confined to edges; the body stays paper.
options.risk: Pastel bands look like a wellness app, not a tracking board.

options.label: Void Queue
options.thesis: Shipments as ivory bitmap lines on an emissive black void; rank is depth.
options.viewport: One still ivory line of the selected tracking number; others drift behind.
options.case: Demo-scene void fights shipment facts, map, and travel history.
options.kept: Selected shipment is the still front plane; others recede.
options.risk: No boxes means facts and a map have nowhere to live.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscope on a signal bench
options.thesis: Live status as a phosphor trace on a ten-division graticule.
options.viewport: A locked green course trace; shipment facts as amber readouts below the graticule.
options.case: A waveform is not a multi-shipment company board with a geographic map.
options.kept: Live route as a persistent triggered trace on a measured grid.
options.risk: Lab-bench theater that cannot hold Google Map geography.

options.label: J-Card Log
options.thesis: Travel history as a timed tracklist ruled in ballpoint.
options.viewport: Side A shipments / Side B history on one folded inlay with running times.
options.case: Mixtape ritual does not identify as freight tracking.
options.kept: Timed sequential list that fills its allotted space exactly.
options.risk: Cute ephemera that undercuts live FedEx truth.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean logistics dashboard: shipment cards, status chips, a map pane, and a timeline, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Top nav, shipment list, detail split with map and history — the arrangement every tracking SaaS ships.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
